entries.reason: The flagged http:// is an example value, an RFC 1918 LAN address with port 5000, inside the HTML comment at hmi/index.html:7-13 that documents the optional dda-api-base meta tag for detached HMI hosting. It is not a network request: the meta content is empty, meaning same-origin (hmi/index.html:14), and the page loads its module script from a same-origin path (hmi/index.html:18). Recorded under R3.1 per R13.2. R13 investigation: the documented :5000 origin is the LocalServer's plaintext listener, which runs only when station authorization is disabled; with authorization enabled the LocalServer serves TLS on :5443 (src/backend/app.py:385-396). hmi/src/api/base.ts accepts http or https bases, and a bare port inherits the page's own scheme. Rewriting the example to https:// would misdocument the :5000 listener and change no request; forcing HTTPS on that device-local HTTP-only listener is the R4 device-local case and is not needed to close this finding. entries.reason: scanner-x/sns-topic-encryption flags the same unencrypted topic as CKV_AWS_26 (Scanner-X's rule set is not public, so its check could not be run locally; it is expected to clear with the same KmsMasterKeyId). Traced to compute-stack.ts:3448-3451: the ComputeStack creates dda-portal-training-alerts without a masterKey, so the deployed topic has no server-side encryption and the Baseline_Template mirrors it with no KmsMasterKeyId. Publishers are two same-account Lambda execution roles only: TrainingEventsHandler and CompilationEventsHandler, granted by trainingAlertTopic.grantPublish at compute-stack.ts:3473 and :3497 and calling sns.publish at training_events.py:221 and :271 and compilation_events.py:200. No AWS service publishes to it: nothing in the repo attaches a CloudWatch alarm action, an EventBridge SnsTopic target, or an S3 notification to trainingAlertTopic, and the exported ARN (CfnOutput TrainingAlertTopicArn, export EdgeCVPortalTrainingAlertTopicArn, compute-stack.ts:3946-3950) has no importer in the repo. Because no service principal publishes, the AWS managed key alias/aws/sns meets R14.1 without locking out a publisher (the R14.2 customer-managed-key case does not arise). Adding KmsMasterKeyId to AWS::SNS::Topic is an in-place, no-interruption update that keeps the topic name, ARN and its out-of-band subscriptions (R16.2). Residual risk / existing control: If an out-of-band AWS service publisher exists, alias/aws/sns would reject it; the design should confirm there is none before choosing the AWS managed key. An owner decision applies (see owner_decisions). Evidence: edge-cv-portal/infrastructure/lib/compute-stack.ts:3448-3451 topic has no masterKey; edge-cv-portal/infrastructure/lib/compute-stack.ts:3473, edge-cv-portal/infrastructure/lib/compute-stack.ts:3497 grantPublish to the two Lambda roles.

LocalServer bedrock_inference Payload_Reference fetch; the URL comes from the untrusted trigger payload. In place: the dispatcher sends only http:// and https:// values to urlopen (payload_fetch.py:236-245), file:// reads require an explicit allow-list root and are realpath-confined (payload_fetch.py:421-437), and the node's allowed_uri_prefixes gate runs before the fetch (payload_fetch.py:241). Gaps against R9: (1) urlopen uses the default opener, which follows HTTP redirects to http, https and ftp targets without re-checking the scheme or the allowed prefixes (R9.1, R9.3); (2) rejection and fetch errors echo the full source URL (payload_fetch.py:282, 309, 317), which can carry userinfo or presigned-URL credential query parameters into the run's per-node error record (R9.4); (3) no test shows unsupported schemes, redirects or credential-bearing URLs being rejected or redacted (R9.5). Fix keeps http(s), S3, file and base64 sources working: an opener with only HTTP/HTTPS handlers whose redirect hook re-applies the scheme and prefix checks, plus URL redaction in error text. Deliberate user-visible change to record: error messages show the URL without userinfo and query, and redirects that leave the allow-list now fail.
deliberate_changes: URLs in payload reference errors and in the run log's Payload_Reference line are redacted to scheme://host[:port]/path: user information and the fragment are dropped, a query becomes ?<redacted>, and exception text appended to a fetch error has those parts removed.

A redirect is followed only to http or https, inside the node's allowed_uri_prefixes (an empty list still admits any remote source), without an https to http downgrade and without user information. Any other redirect, for every status the runtime follows (301, 302, 303, 307, and 308 on Python 3.11), fails the node's Payload_Reference with an error naming the rejected scheme or the redacted destination, and its target isn't requested.

An http(s) Payload_Reference URL with user information is refused before any request (URLs with embedded credentials are not supported). Such URLs never fetched, because urllib doesn't send URL user information as credentials.

entries.reason: B301 at the dill.load call: dill deserializer in the offline, operator-invoked legacy reference-image-map migration CLI. The inference path never imports this module (supervised_bbox_stage1_postprocessor.py:62-77 reads only the JSON + NumPy format) and the migration writes only JSON and np.save(allow_pickle=False) output (reference_image_map_io.py:91-94), which satisfies R10.2's no-new-pickle clause. Gap: the input path comes straight from argv and is opened with no check that it lies in a location the component owns or that a less-privileged process cannot write it; the trust boundary is documentation only (module docstring). R10.1/R10.2 require the read to be confined to component-owned locations. The rule the design adopted (R10 change): open_trusted_legacy_map resolves the path, requires it strictly below one of the two TRUSTED_LEGACY_MAP_ROOTS (/aws_dda/greengrass/v2/packages/artifacts-unarchived and /aws_dda/dda_triton/triton_model_repo), opens it with O_NOFOLLOW, and loads only from a descriptor that is a regular file owned by root or the effective uid, with no group or other write bit; the check applies to the opened file itself, not to its directories. The utility keeps working for its documented one-time use. This copy ships in every LocalServer flask-app image (src/backend/Dockerfile:127 and the jp5/jp6/jp7/x86_64_nvidia variants).

entries.reason: PRIORITY (R6): a real gap in the code, currently not reachable through any deployed API. (1) No allow decision or identity uses unverified claims: handler (lines 282-345) builds userId, email, username, role, groups and the Allow policy only from validate_jwt_token's return value, which is the signature-verified decode at lines 185-195 (RS256 only, line 188; key taken from the configured Cognito pool's JWKS or from an exact ISSUER_WHITELIST entry, lines 164-169). (2) Signature: verified. (3) Expiry: verify_exp is on (line 192), but PyJWT checks exp only when the claim is present, and exp is not required, so a token without exp would pass. (4) Issuer: the unverified iss (line 159) picks the JWKS, which R6.2 allows as key selection, but it is also passed as the expected issuer (line 190), so the issuer check compares the token with itself, and the Cognito branch matches by substring (line 164). The signature check still pins tokens to configured key sets, but R6.2 and R6.3 require the expected issuer to come from configuration. (5) Audience or client: the deployed function sets ALLOWED_AUDIENCES to an empty string (edge-cv-portal/infrastructure/lib/compute-stack.ts:1268), which turns verify_aud off (line 193). Any token the user pool signs, for any app client and either token type, is accepted, so R6.3 is unmet. (6) Exposure: JwtAuthorizerHandler is created (compute-stack.ts:1259-1272) but nothing references it. Every Portal REST API uses API Gateway's CognitoUserPoolsAuthorizer (for example api-gateway-stack.ts:146), and the infrastructure has no TokenAuthorizer, RequestAuthorizer or CfnAuthorizer. (7) Strict audience check: the user pool has one app client, dda-portal-client (edge-cv-portal/infrastructure/lib/auth-stack.ts:89). The frontend sends the ID token (edge-cv-portal/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:90-92, edge-cv-portal/frontend/src/services/api.ts:1325-1329), whose aud is that client id, so pinning the allow-list to that id would not break it. Cognito access tokens carry client_id instead of aud, and an aud-only check rejects them (PyJWT raises on a missing aud once an audience is set). If access tokens must work, check aud for token_use=id and client_id for token_use=access against the same list. No other app client is defined in CDK or created at runtime (searched). Because nothing invokes the authorizer, no current client breaks either way. Remediation keeps function: expected issuer from configuration with an exact match; the allow-list wired from the user-pool client id; exp required; only the token header is read before verification, and only its kid, to select a key, and the unverified payload decode is deleted; tests for tampered, expired, wrong-issuer, wrong-audience and valid tokens (R6.5). Existing tests cover only the valid and tampered cases (test/backend-test/security/preservation/test_preservation_secrets_jwt.py:417-458). Found during task 1: at 4a3f960 construct_rsa_key called serialize(), which cryptography's RSA public key doesn't provide (the jwt layer pins cryptography 50.0.1), so the deployed function denied every token before its signature check; task 1 builds the PEM with public_bytes() (deliberate change 5).
